key_insight: A mesh-free deep energy method predicts thermally driven crack nucleation, spacing, propagation and arrest without prescribing crack paths or nucleation sites.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports thermal-shock fracture analysis where evolving thermal boundary layers and unknown crack paths complicate mesh-based simulation.
method: Separate multiresolution neural representations model displacement and phase fields, and transient temperature.
Minimize mechanical energy and a backward Euler thermal functional using integration points resampled each iteration.
Restrict irreversibility to the crack set, retain optimizer state across load steps and decay learning rates within each step.
evidence_signal: Tests show close agreement with finite element initiation peak loads on two notched plates, a glass-strip oscillation threshold near linear stability predictions and ceramic-slab crack spacing near a published benchmark.
watch_item: Crack arrays in the slab and annulus are denser than finite element predictions on the same material field, leaving a discrepancy that warrants further validation.
paper_title: A mesh-free deep energy method for phase-field modeling of thermally driven brittle fracture
